stories.title: Trump resists AI slowdown as the political tide turns
stories.simple_summary: Donald Trump is pushing back against calls for slowing down AI development. Political leaders are split on whether AI should grow faster or slower.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly involves politicians disagreeing — it doesn't immediately affect your daily life or business, though government rules on AI could matter later.

stories.title: Select committee calls for bill to address AI threat to human rights
stories.simple_summary: A group of lawmakers wants to create new rules to make sure AI systems don't harm people's rights and freedoms. They're calling for new laws to protect citizens.
stories.why_it_matters: If these rules pass, they could affect how companies use AI systems that might collect your information or make decisions about you.

stories.title: Dreamforce welcomes more than 43,000 to San Francisco amid debate over pace of AI development
stories.simple_summary: A big tech company conference in San Francisco drew over 43,000 people, but attendees are debating whether AI is being developed too fast or too slow.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly about tech industry insiders discussing their field — nothing you need to act on unless you work in technology.

stories.title: What Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei Argued in His Call for AI Slowdown
stories.simple_summary: The leader of an AI company published an open letter saying the industry should slow down and be more careful about how fast it builds AI systems.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly interesting to investors and tech workers — it doesn't directly change how you'll use AI in your daily life or small business.

stories.title: House Speaker Johnson says Congress shouldn't lead AI safety efforts
stories.simple_summary: The Speaker of the House said Congress shouldn't be the ones making decisions about AI safety rules. He thinks others should handle it instead.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a political position that might eventually affect what rules get made about AI, but nothing immediate for you to worry about.

stories.title: Top Lawmakers Agree A.I.’s Risks Are Rising but Say They Have No Quick Fix
stories.simple_summary: Top lawmakers agree that AI could create problems, but they say they don't have easy answers or quick fixes for those problems yet.
stories.why_it_matters: This is honest talk from politicians — they're basically saying AI rules are complicated and will take time to figure out.

stories.title: Trump and Mike Johnson think the AI industry is overreacting
stories.simple_summary: Some important AI company leaders want to slow down AI development, but Trump and the House Speaker disagree and think the industry is overreacting.
stories.why_it_matters: This is political and business debate at the highest level — nothing that changes what you need to do right now.

stories.title: What’s behind the AI industry’s latest warnings of doom?
stories.simple_summary: AI industry leaders are publicly debating whether AI might pose serious dangers to humanity, with some calling it an existential threat.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly academics and tech leaders discussing long-term risks — not something affecting your immediate use of AI tools.

stories.title: Chip Roy is leaving Congress — but not before warning his colleagues about AI
stories.simple_summary: A congressman who is leaving office is warning his colleagues that they should pay attention to AI and its potential problems.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a politician's warning to other politicians — it's a signal that some lawmakers think Congress needs to take AI seriously.

stories.title: Obama urges Democrats to have a ‘clear plan’ for AI safeguards
stories.simple_summary: Former President Obama says Democrats should make AI regulation and safety a top priority and create a clear plan for how to handle it.
stories.why_it_matters: This means one major political party thinks AI safety matters — it could eventually lead to new rules, but that takes time.

stories.title: What are the five pros and cons of artificial intelligence?
stories.simple_summary: This article lists good things and bad things about artificial intelligence. (The headline alone doesn't tell us what those are.)
stories.why_it_matters: A general article explaining AI's benefits and downsides — useful background information but no news about what's happening now.

stories.title: AI will transform capitalism – but how?
stories.simple_summary: AI will probably change how our economy and businesses work, but it's unclear exactly how that transformation will happen.
stories.why_it_matters: This is thinking about the big economic future — interesting to consider, but too vague to know what to do about it today.
